items.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: I first was with Jeanne Lee, that was the first New York job I ever had.

ctx.x: But I mean musically, is it possible to put a description on the kind of music.

Well I was fresh in New York so I was open to everything. I had joined Cecil McBee’s band, I was playing also with Mickey Bass, you know, and I got the job with McBee’s band — well actually I first was with Jeanne Lee, that was the first New York job I ever © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

had. She passed away not too long ago. And Henry Threadgill had that job and he needed to go back to Chicago for something and he asked me to fill in for him and I did, and it was a great success and so they extended us another week. So I was with her. While I was doing that I was you know, just getting around New York, getting around, learning people, hanging out and meeting people. I then sat in with Mickey Bass and got hired to play. He had a month of Sundays and so after the Jeanne Lee thing, and so I was…
